slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The essay's country table says rural registry offices (it names Hlatikhulu, Hluti and Nhlangano) work a hybrid: informants bring a chief's or indvuna's letter, officers fill the paper BMD-1 form by hand, and typists then enter the data into the National Population Register over networked terminals; it gives no date for the practice, so the essay's published date of 31 March 2026 is used.

The essay's country table describes electronic entry of births, from the BMD-1 form, into the National Population Register at registry offices, and speaks more broadly of 'vital events' without naming deaths; undated, so the published date of 31 March 2026 is used.

The essay's country table states that all district-level civil registration offices countrywide, rural ones included, have digitised databases with electronic entry of vital events; it gives no count of offices and no year, so the published date of 31 March 2026 is used.
The essay's country table cites a national CRVS plan for 2022-27 that pushes integration and mobile units, and a 2024 tender for a further digital roadmap.

systems.owner: civil registration offices (CRD); ministry not named
systems.tiers: all district-level civil registration offices countrywide, including rural ones such as Hlatikhulu, Hluti and Nhlangano, by networked terminals
health facilities, said to be 'linked via CMIS' while registration takes place at civil registration offices
